summary: R. Gayathri is an Indologist who studied as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).

R. Gordon Wasson (1898–1986) worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism, LSE, and Columbia University, later working as a journalist, at Guaranty Trust, and at J.P. Morgan & Co. (1934–1963).

R. H. Blyth (1898–1964) was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of London (~1919–1923), he held posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1925–1940) and Kanazawa University (~1940–1941), and taught Robert Baker Aitken.

R. H. Tawney (1880–1962) was a historian who studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1899–1903). He held academic posts at the University of Glasgow (~1906–1908) and the London School of Economics (~1913–1949).
R. N. Gadre was an Indologist attested in 1959 as Professor of Sanskrit at both Sir Parashurambhau College and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

R. Sathyanarayana (1927–2020) was an Indologist who earned a master's in chemistry at the University of Mysore. He taught at Sarada Vilas College (1949–1984) and served as President of the Indian Music Congress.

R. Thangaswami Sarma (1924–2000) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Annamalai University and Madras Sanskrit College. He held posts at Presidency College, Chennai, the University of Madras, Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and Adyar Library (1994–2000).

R. Venkatraman completed his PhD (1975–1980) at Madurai Kamaraj University under N. Subrahmanian and N. Jagadeesan, later serving there as Reader (attested 1990) in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology.
Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) was a philosopher who studied at University College London (~1878–1880). He founded Visva-Bharati University and the Sino-Indian Cultural Society.
Rachael Wiseman is a philosopher who studied at the University of York (~2005–2009). She was appointed as a lecturer at the University of Liverpool around 2014.

Rachel H. Pang is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia and served as Lester D. Coltrane III Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Davidson College (attested 2019).

Rachelle M. Scott specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her dissertation at Northwestern University under George D. Bond and Robert Launay, and held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2009–2017).

Radha Krishna Choudhary (1921–1985) was an Indologist and historian educated at Patna University. He served at Ganesh Dutt College, Shankar Sah Vikramshila Mahavidyalaya, and Tilka Manjhi Bhagalpur University (1974–1984), and founded the K. P. Jayaswal Archaeological Museum.

Radha Kumud Mukherjee (1884–1963) was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1901–1905). He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1916–1917), Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1917–1921), and the University of Mysore (~1917–1921).

Radhika Herzberger (1938–) is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Toronto (~1976–1982) under Bimal Krishna Matilal and became Director of Rishi Valley School around 1982.

Rafal Stepien earned his PhD at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü and Bernard Faure (attested 2015). Active in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he held posts at Wadham College, Oxford (2012–2013) and Harvard University (attested 2015).
Rafał Felbur works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He was a PhD candidate at Stanford University (attested 2015) supervised by Paul Harrison, and also studied under John R. McRae and Luis O. Gómez.
Raffaele Torella (1950–) is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Raniero Gnoli (~1970–1976). He served as a faculty member at Sapienza University of Rome (~1980–2020).
Raffaello Orlando is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at Princeton University under Denis Twitchett by 1981.

Raghu Vira (1902–1963) studied at University of the Punjab and Leiden University. A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, he headed the Sanskrit Department at Sanatan Dharma College and founded the International Academy of Indian Culture (1932).
